correctness.rationale: The seed attachment probabilities follow by splitting on the sampled vertex. A star must be centered at one of the seeds because their edge persists. Each star orientation has mass 1/(m-1), and from it the unique seed leaf becomes a second hub with probability 1/[m(m-1)], giving total entrance mass 2/[m(m-1)^2]. Interior survival is at least (m-2)/m per step. Substitution of g(k+1)/g(k)=1-1/[k(k+1)] shows that the killed transition of g(a)g(b) equals (1-2/m)g(a)g(b) minus the two positive cross terms displayed. The weight is at least one and starts at K g(m-2). The telescoping product and sum therefore give both finite bounds, including the empty-product case n=4. The logarithm of the product tail is O(1/k), so the upper sum differs from the lower harmonic sum by O(1), which suffices for the normalized bounds and conditional probability. At n=4 and n=5 the recurrence gives R_n=1/6 and 13/72. Inspected but did not execute checker.py; its recorded 720 finite checks are corroboration only. No limit for the normalized constant was inferred.
